Compare short sequence patterns between groups of sessions

Source: R/sequence_compare_htna.R
sequence_compare_htna.Rd

sequence_compare_htna() compares short sequence patterns between the cohorts of a grouped htna network, or between the groups of a single network given by group. It counts every k-gram (a run of k consecutive codes) in each group and finds the patterns that are more or less frequent in a group than expected if pattern and group were independent. Each pattern gets a standardized residual per group (Haberman, 1973) and, optionally, a permutation test (the session is the unit) or a chi-square test of whether its frequency differs between the groups, with p-values adjusted across all patterns. Two groups of sessions can differ not only in single transitions but in longer runs of codes, such as a human request followed by an AI plan and an AI execution.

With level = "type" every code is first replaced by its actor type, so the patterns are meta-paths such as Human->AI->Human and the comparison shows how the turn-taking between actors differs between the groups. sequence_compare_htna() runs Nestimate's sequence_compare() on the sequences and returns a net_sequence_comparison object.

For single transitions use permutation_htna() or mosaic_plot_htna(); for descriptive counts of patterns in one network use extract_meta_paths().

Usage

sequence_compare_htna(x, group = NULL, level = c("state", "type"), ...)

Arguments

x

A grouped htna network (an htna_group), or an htna network together with group.

group

The grouping of the sessions when x is a single network (default NULL).

level

"state" (default) compares patterns of codes; "type" compares patterns of actor types.

...

Settings: sub (pattern lengths, default 3:5), min_freq (minimum count in every group, 5), test ("permutation", "chisq" or "none"), iter (permutations, 1000), adjust (multiplicity correction, "fdr") and actor (needs Nestimate 1.0.19 or later).

Value

An object of class net_sequence_comparison with print(), summary() and plot() methods. summary() returns a data frame with one row per pattern and columns pattern, length, one freq_<group>, prop_<group> and resid_<group> column per group, effect_size and, when a test is run, p_value.

Conditions

An error of class htna_bad_input when level = "type" and x has no actor partition.

References

Haberman, S. J. (1973). The analysis of residuals in cross-classified tables. Biometrics, 29(1), 205-220. doi:10.2307/2529686

See also

extract_meta_paths(), permutation_htna(), mosaic_plot_htna().

Examples

data(human_ai)
grp <- build_htna(human_ai, actor_type = "actor_type", group = "phase")
#> Metadata aggregated per session: ties resolved by first occurrence in 'cluster' (24 sessions), 'actor_type' (9 sessions)
#> Metadata aggregated per session: ties resolved by first occurrence in 'session_date' (1 sessions), 'cluster' (18 sessions), 'actor_type' (15 sessions)
# iter = 50 keeps the example fast; use the default 1000 in practice.
sequence_compare_htna(grp, iter = 50)
